It doesn't really change anything for Fedora, because Fedora puts `mz_compat.h` in `/usr/include/minizip/mz_compat.h` but doesn't put it in `/usr/include/minizip-ng`

It looks like the way that they've done it is that they have essentially two minizip-ng packages, one built with the compatibility layer that also gets a directory structure that makes it automatically be found by packages looking for the original minizip, without having to update it. The minizip-ng directories only have the newer, non backwards compatible API.

They can do that because they don't have to worry about parallel installs.

So I guess it doesn't matter too much, other than confusing people, because we'll find minizip-ng with the compatibility layer and use it, calling it minizip (and saying we didn't find -ng).

Yes, but if we want to offer the new compression metods it gets tricky(?)
But no big deal atm I suppose.

skrev:

I guess I'm surprised nothing else is broken with a new brew install. :-)  
  
For Windows builds, the library versions are controlled.  
  
This seems like a breaking change but maybe stable going forward?  
https://github.com/zlib-ng/minizip-ng/commit/7df56f7cc8438b1b67c881cad049b29bf075bccd

> This seems like a breaking change but maybe stable going forward?

It's not entirely a breaking change, because the `zip.h` and `unzip.h` files always existed, containing the same thing as the `mz_compat.h` header (those `configure_file` statements just copy).  Those files have been generated since at least minizip 2.10.2 (using configure_file since 3.0.5):

https://github.com/zlib-ng/minizip-ng/commit/4c886bd5ab4ac646f89706ef3fc0dd4ff3285ee5

https://github.com/zlib-ng/minizip-ng/commit/3ac4d741b334ccfc6c733e7ea5918e39f78202df

So we probably could just include zip.h or unzip.h from the appropriate directory, as we're using the compatibility mode. It would be easiest in one sense didn't do the parent directory manipulations and just included the file, but other libraries (including libzip) can have a "zip.h" or "unzip.h" so I suppose we do that to reduce the chance of including the wrong file. We could save off a variable name.

The only place where minizip is used right now is supporting zipped configuration directories. (People would like to be able to treat zip archives of capture files as file sets, I guess.)

On Linux and macOS, we also don't I think need to do the searches for the LZMA, Zstd, etc. libraries, unless we're linking against the static library (and pkg-config gives all the information about which static libraries we would need to link against, including possibly openSSL.)
